release-deployment-safety.why: this change cuts a release: it bumps the version across every location and folds the pending changelog fragments into a new immutable section, and 1.3.3 is a patch because nothing in the four folded changes turns a currently-green consumer red (ADR-0113's consumerRequiredGates are classified but esk-genesis installs only manifest.gates+machinery into a consumer; ADR-0111/0112 fix the generator; the overclaim fix is docs).
release-deployment-safety.what: bumped VERSION, package.json, package-lock.json, and gate-manifest.json (version and generatedFrom) to 1.3.3; ran scripts/changelog-release.mjs 1.3.3 2026-11-03 to fold the four fragments oldest-first into a new CHANGELOG.md section and empty changelog.d; chose patch per the semver rule in ADR-0049.
quotes: Every change must be independently deployable, backward-compatible, observable while it rolls out

skeptical-audit.why: the semver claim (that 1.3.3 is a safe patch) is the kind of assertion that must be checked against the evidence, not assumed: each folded fragment was read for a consumer-affecting change, and the version consistency across all four files was verified rather than presumed.
skeptical-audit.what: verified every version location reads 1.3.3 and that the folded changes do not tighten or remove an installed consumer gate or change the manifest shape a consumer enforces; recorded the patch decision with that evidence.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: the release edits the gate manifest (its version and generatedFrom) and the changelog, so it got a fresh-context review of every changed file against the four questions, with version consistency across the locations as the adversarial focus.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context subagent review of the release diff; it checked that all version files agree on 1.3.3, that manifest integrity still passes, and that no folded change forces consumer action; the review entry is recorded in docs/arch-reviews/entries/.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

architectural-decision-records.why: no new architectural decision; the release follows the existing governance in ADR-0049 (how releases are cut and versioned), and a routine version bump needs no new ADR.

pattern-selector.why: no feature, class, module, or data flow is designed or changed; a version bump and changelog fold selects no pattern.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system, service, schema, or algorithm is designed or changed; the manifest's shape is unchanged, only its version string.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: no behavior changes; the release folds already-reviewed changelog text and bumps version strings, so there is no new use case to enumerate.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: no code or test surface changes; the existing suite still runs in CI on the release branch.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no input, auth, secret, dependency, or network surface changes; version strings and changelog text only.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service, endpoint, SLO, or alert; publishing a release artifact is covered by release-deployment-safety, not operational readiness of a service.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data, and no storage, retention, migration, or backup surface.

arch-encode.why: no caught mistake to encode as a rule; this is a routine release cut.

verifiable-quality-gates.why: no automated check is added or changed; the existing gates run unchanged against the release branch.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; metadata and Markdown only.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user interactive surface; the changelog is plain-language release notes, not a UI.
